chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from his father who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about a man who fasts in Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'They are the two months that Allah, the Exalted, said: two consecutive months, as a repentance from Allah.' I said, 'So he does not separate between them?' He said, 'If he breaks the fast during the night, that is a separation.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'No continuous fasting (Wisal) in fasting,' meaning a man does not fast two consecutive days without breaking the fast. And it is recommended for the servant not to leave the pre-dawn meal (Suhoor). The book of Fasting from al-Istibsar is completed.

key_terms.الاسْتِبْصَار: Al-Istibsar (one of the Four Books of Shia hadith, compiled by al-Tusi)
key_terms.السَّحُور: Al-Suhoor (the pre-dawn meal before fasting begins)
key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, month of fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.وِصَال: Visal (continuous fasting for two or more days without breaking the fast at night)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting continuously from Sha'ban into Ramadan without breaking the fast at night?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that fasting in Sha'ban and Ramadan are two consecutive months of repentance. He explains that breaking the fast at night (Iftar) serves as a separation (Fasl) between the two months, preventing the prohibition of 'Visal' (continuous fasting without breaking the fast). It is also recommended to not neglect the pre-dawn meal (Suhoor).
